4. Macroscopic projection costs exponentially little
----------------------------------------------------
The product number distribution is Poisson-binomial with independent
Bernoulli parameters rho_i. Its mean divided by L tends to mu>0 and
variance V_L=sum rho_i(1-rho_i) satisfies V_L/L->v>0. Choose any fixed
eps<=mu/4, later reduced if necessary for the dilute comparator, and
P_hi=1_{N>floor(eps L)}. Let q_L=||P_hi psi_L||^2 and p_L=1-q_L.

For large L the mean is at least mu L/2. The centered Bernoulli log
moment generating function has second derivative at most1/4 (it is the
variance of a tilted Bernoulli), so its value is at most t^2/8. The usual
Chernoff optimization consequently gives

 p_L<=exp[-2(mu L/4)^2/(L-1)]<=exp[-mu^2 L/8].            (4.1)

This proves the needed tail without an iid-parameter assumption.
The exact norm bound, including all sites, is
 ||B_L||<=4J L^3+(kappa+|lambda|)L.                      (4.2)
Each exchange bond has norm4J and both endpoint fields total norm4J;
W,N have norm at most L. N commutes with B_L, so cross terms between
the two projections vanish EXACTLY. For psi_hi=P_hi psi_L/sqrt(q_L),

 <psi_hi,B_L psi_hi>
 =(<psi_L,B_L psi_L>-p_L<psi_lo,B_L psi_lo>)/q_L
 <=[C_theta/L+p_L||B_L||]/q_L=O(1/L)+O(L^3e^{-cL})=o(1). (4.3)

Thus projection costs probability times the norm, rather than its square
root; it does not silently alter the Hamiltonian or divide by a rare
macro probability. The low component may have either energy sign.

5. Sector anti-concentration and weighted Jensen yield sqrt(L)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Let p_m=||1_{N=m}psi_L||^2. Fourier inversion and the characteristic
function of the independent Bernoulli variables give

 |product_i(1-rho_i+rho_i e^{it})|
 <=exp[-2V_L sin^2(t/2)]<=exp[-2V_L t^2/pi^2], |t|<=pi,
 p_max:=max_m p_m
 <=(2pi)^{-1}int_{-pi}^{pi}exp[-2V_L t^2/pi^2]dt
 <=sqrt(pi)/(2sqrt(2V_L)).                              (5.1)

The first inequality uses sqrt(1-x)<=exp(-x/2), the second
sin(|t|/2)>=|t|/pi. This is a rigorous uniform anti-concentration bound
with all parameters possibly different; V_L~vL makes p_max=O(L^-1/2).

For p_m>0 write psi_m=1_{N=m}psi_L/sqrt(p_m), E_m=<psi_m,B_L psi_m>.
In each such sector, the finite-dimensional spectral Jensen inequality
implies Tr_m exp(-tau B_L)>=<psi_m,exp(-tau B_L)psi_m>
                                  >=e

statement.assertion: Z_I=Tr_I exp(-tau B) >= (q/pmax) exp[-tau <psi_I,B psi_I>], psi_I=P_I psi/sqrt q. No upper bound on individual sector energies is required. For Poisson-binomial trial number, pmax<=sqrt(pi)/(2sqrt(2V)) with V=sum rho_i(1-rho_i).
